messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED (P1) - eu-west-1 inference pool: multiple nodes switching to NotReady / kubelet restart loops causing ~5xx spike on hosted API. Affected ASG: infer-eu-west-pool-a. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-node-flap>. Please ack and start triage.

Dina_oncall: acked. I'm taking initial lead. Observed 3 nodes NotReady in eu-west-1a, 2 in eu-west-1b. Traffic still landing; 5xx rate ~9-12% above baseline.

sam_sre: on it — grabbing node events and kubelet logs now. Can someone post recent metric link?

kai_prod_eng: link to dashboards: <https://dashboards.redwood/prod/inference/requests?region=eu-west-1>. Error spike visible since 14:17 UTC. High-volume customers affected (approx 6% of total requests).

ana_runtime: quick note: I'm seeing repeated GPU driver resets and CUDA OOM in kubelet logs on node infer-eu-1a-07:
```
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=23456: Read error logs
kubelet[1]: E0314 14:18:05.123456   12345 kubelet.go:xyz] kubelet runtime service status: error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = containerd: process_exited: exit status 139
containerd: oom-kill event for pid 23456, container_name=redwood-infer
```
Seems like either driver crash or container runtime segfault causing kubelet to restart.

dina_oncall: thanks Ana. First mitigations: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain safe (prefer evict to fallback pool) 3) enable routing fallback to cpu-inference pool for latency-tolerant customers 4) notify status page. I'll run cordon/drain now.

sam_sre: adding commands I ran:
```
# check node status
kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-eu-west -o wide
kubectl describe node infer-eu-1a-07 | egrep "Kubelet|NotReady|Restart"
# drain
kubectl cordon infer-eu-1a-07
kubectl drain infer-eu-1a-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
Drain started on infer-eu-1a-07 — pods are moving to other nodes but some crashloops.

infra-bot: Auto-detected repeated kubelet restarts on 3 nodes in infer-eu-west cluster; created k8s incident ticket INC-4729.

ana_runtime: note: prefix/KV cache is heavy on these pods; evicting and forcing model cache cold start will increase latency but reduce memory pressure. Suggest turning off prefix cache on the affected deployment group temporarily: set env REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE=false for deployment infer-runtime-v2 in eu-west.

dina_oncall: doing that change via API now (quick patch):
```
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/routes/infer-runtime-v2/config \
  -d '{"env":{"REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE":"false"}}'
```
Applied. Will watch memory footprints.

kai_prod_eng: FYI: we've sent affected customers a heads-up via private slack; ops/support to prepare a status page update if this persists.

marta_support: drafted status snippet: "We are investigating increased 5xx errors in eu-west inference endpoints due to node instability. Our engineers are performing mitigation steps; some requests may route to fallback pools. More updates in 30 minutes." Approve?

dina_oncall: approved, post it.

sam_sre: restarted kubelet on infer-eu-1a-07 to see if transient fixes; kubelet came back but flapped again after ~90s with same segfault in containerd. Suspect an underlying OS/kernel issue triggered by driver crash.

ana_runtime: agree. Next move: evict GPU workloads from shaky hosts and taint nodes to prevent scheduling until we patch driver/kernel. I'll apply taint and trigger scaling of cpu-inference pool.

sam_sre: commands I'm applying:
```
kubectl taint nodes infer-eu-1a-07 node.kubernetes.io/unstable=true:NoSchedule
# scale cpu fallback pool
kubectl scale deployment cpu-infer-autoscaler --replicas=8 -n inference
```
Taint applied. CPU fallback scaled.

dina_oncall: also toggled routing policy to prefer dedicated capacity and cpu-infer for new requests. Control plane patch: route preference changed to: [dedicated > cpu-infer > gpu-infer]. Rolling out now.

infra-bot: Control plane route policy updated by dina_oncall (change id rp-8812).

kai_prod_eng: after routing change error rate dropped to +3% over baseline (was +12%). Customer impact reduced but still some spikes.

ana_runtime: ongoing: I'm preparing a node image patch (containerd 1.7.8 + kernel minor) to deploy to affected ASG. Will coordinate a rolling replacement of infer-eu-west-pool-a overnight if stable.

sam_sre: opening proactive smoke checks on newly scheduled pods — seeing some pods land on healthy nodes and run fine. Taking heap profiles from a few pods.

dina_oncall: handoff plan: I need to hand off in ~45m to eli_noc (night SRE). Current state: routing fallback in place, 3 nodes tainted/drained, cpu-infer scaled, patch in progress (ana preparing image). Outstanding: rolling image replacement for the ASG, kernel/driver investigation, postmortem owners. Please escalate if error rate >8% again.

eli_noc: taking handoff at 15:30 UTC. Please paste the exact list of nodes tainted and control-plane change ids.

sam_sre: tainted nodes: infer-eu-1a-07, infer-eu-1a-09, infer-eu-1b-03. Control-plane change ids: rp-8812 (routing), cfg-4421 (prefix_cache toggle).

dina_oncall: leaving notes: logs collected at /internal/incident/INC-4729/logs.tar.gz, heap dumps at /internal/incident/INC-4729/heap/, driver panic traces attached. Oncall checklist completed partially: notify customers (done), apply routing fallback (done), scale fallback (done), taint/drain (done), prepare image (in progress).

incident-bot: Update: Severity remains P1. Next automated status update scheduled in 30 minutes.

eli_noc: acknowledged. I'll monitor and coordinate the rolling replacement overnight if needed. If anything spikes back >10% ping me and I'll escalate to infra team. :eyes:
